title: Prove sharp P104 temporal rank bound and correction-budget obstruction
body:
The native P104 `G/2` channel leaves `I-G/2` unimplemented. This contribution proves that **no linear redesign using the frozen chronological common-frame access can complete identity transfer**: a sharp eight-register cut limits source-to-target rank to `8D`, versus the required `104D`.

The new package `research/p104-temporal-cut-obstruction/` adds a written proof, exact source-bound certificate and independently implemented forward/reverse checkers. It saturates all common-frame communication at all 4,059 event boundaries, so the result covers arbitrary coefficients, extra same-frame gates and helper/target mixing, beyond the predecessor's particular scalar word. The original `G/2` channel attains the bound.

For corrections inserted between original events that **restore every frame before the next original event**, retain the original transports and add no storage lifetimes, the cut proves at least **96 additional positive-rank transports per call**. Under the explicitly conditional fully hosted four-pair, nine-stage coverage contract, only `328/9` rank units per call remain; the completed zero-saving moment is at least **7659/7592 > 1**, independently of idle packing. As a concrete accounting illustration,208 added ranks/call imply a zero-saving moment of `7785/7592 > 1` under this contract; a fixed-coverage calculator cannot treat the added cost as free displacement of idle mass without a separate realization argument. Persistent changed-frame buffers, retiming, replacement/fusion of existing transports, new storage and changed global coverage are outside that corollary.

This resolves a defined part of the revision-4 `p104-side-correction` priority and identifies the access/scheduling premise a successful completion must change. **No new kappa, supplier admission, selected-frontier change or universal P104 barrier.**

Validation:
- Registered Python 3.12.14 replay and metadata/source pins pass.
- Exact E8 reconstruction, `G²=26G`, `(I-G/2)⁻¹=I-G/24`, and all 280 arbitrary-input columns including dirty restoration.
- Intact graph and all eight single-edge restorations; seven rejecting semantic/schema controls and basis-order invariance.
- Separate read-only replay from a source export without Git; all 14 files unchanged.
- Independent AI code/proof review and optimized Python 3.14.7 replay pass. No human review or proof-assistant formalization claimed.

Reproduce:
```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/p104-temporal-cut-obstruction/verify.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-temporal-cut-obstruction
```

Started from canonical main `564148b82ae9df72163f22106f15e73efca8aff2`. Exact source pins, overlap coverage, environment and open next questions are in the package. Native Clifford recompilation, chronological owner construction, all-size/precision/outer transfer and the selected full cold replay are not newly established or run; selected and frozen predecessor files are untouched.

Credit: Rohan Arun / #1972 (scalar/frame channel), Chafik Boukhalfa / #1991 (native realization), Adam Gall / #1940 (schedule), with P104 geometry/decoder and coverage predecessors credited in the README. The concurrent [final-query-cut correction claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1167#discussioncomment-18931651) is acknowledged; this is a complementary structural obstruction, not a duplicate construction or audit of unpublished work.

Prepared for David Arias with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0.
